title: Assert persisted state before a later step in the test overwrites it
rule: When a test proves what one step persists for a later run (the last session a quit records, a cache, a ledger), check it right after that step: restart and read it back, or read the stored rows, before the test calls anything that rewrites the same state (a second quit, a resume, another save). A later step that replaces the table hides a regression in the first one. Prove the test by breaking the first step's filter and seeing it fail.
rationale: E29.3 (#184): the quit test for document-scoped faces ran restore_session and a second shutdown before restarting, and the second shutdown replaced last_session, so a first shutdown that remembered document-only faces still passed.
